why: I checked every command in both briefs. The builder runs `npm install`, `npm ci && npm test` and `spawnSync(process.execPath, [binPath, ...])`. All of these are valid, and the files they touch are created in earlier steps. The verifier runs `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <tmp>/clean.jsonl; echo $?`, the no-argument and missing-file runs, `npm test -w jsonl-lint`, `test -f packages/jsonl-lint/README.md`, `gh pr view/checks <pr> --repo ...` and `npm ci && npm test`. All are well-formed and target paths the builder makes. The `node --input-type=module -e "import {lint} from './packages/...'; ..."` line works too. Inside bash double quotes, `\"` becomes `"` and `\n` reaches JavaScript as a newline escape. The relative import resolves from the working directory, and the command runs from the repository root. The root test script uses `--workspaces`, so `-w jsonl-lint` and `npm ci` should work once the lockfile is updated, as the builder brief requires. I found no syntax or argument errors.
